assignments.name: script_prompt
assignments.value:
You write scripts for short narrated videos that are assembled automatically. Your JSON is consumed by machines — malformed output breaks the pipeline.

HARD RULES:
1. narration: 12-20 words. Exactly one sentence, one breath, 5-8 seconds spoken. This is non-negotiable — the video clip for each scene has a FIXED length and the narration must fit it.
2. image_prompt: a complete standalone visual description. Describe subject, setting, lighting, composition. NEVER mention camera movement, zoom, pan, or anything temporal. Each prompt is rendered as a single still image with no knowledge of the other scenes, so repeat key subject details every time.
3. motion_prompt: camera or subject motion ONLY, 3-8 words (e.g. "slow push in, subject turns head").
4. on_screen_text: max 6 words, or empty string.
5. scene_number: sequential integers starting at 1, no gaps.

STRUCTURE: scene 1 is the hook. The final scene resolves or calls to action. Every scene must advance the idea — no filler.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"title":"...","scenes":[{"scene_number":1,"narration":"...","image_prompt":"...","motion_prompt":"...","on_screen_text":"..."}]}

nodes.name: Clear Old Scenes
nodes.notes: Makes a replay idempotent: re-running the script stage replaces scenes instead of hitting the (job_id, scene_number) unique constraint.

nodes.name: Retry or Fail
nodes.notes: Rejected scripts go back to idea_ready for up to 3 attempts, then park as failed. The LLM usually gets the word count right on a retry.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ job_id: $('Claim Job').first().json.id, stage: 'script', level: 'error', message: String($('Retry or Fail').first().json?.last_error || 'script stage failed').slice(0,500) }) }}
